biography: John Rawls was an American political philosopher whose work reshaped debates about justice, fairness, and democratic legitimacy. In A Theory of Justice, he asks which principles free and equal persons could accept under fair conditions. His method of reflective equilibrium moves between considered judgments, principles, arguments, and relevant background knowledge, allowing each to be revised. PHIL 123 uses that method less as a recipe for agreement than as a disciplined way to make changes in judgment visible and answerable.

teaching.whyThisPerson: Rawls gives the course its central model of considered judgment under pressure: reflective equilibrium.
